correctness.rationale: The adjacent pair gcds are gcd(n+1,3) and gcd(n+2,3), so the triple gcd is one. For the outer pair the four cross-factor gcds multiply since n and 2n−1, and n+2 and 2n+3, are coprime within their own factorizations. This gives gcd(n,2) gcd(n,3) gcd(n+2,5) and hence d≤30. The increasing generators are minimal for n≥4 by the stated inequalities and 2n²−9n−6≠0 (nonsquare discriminant 129); (6,15,28) is minimal, and n=3 gives the symmetric two-generator semigroup <15,28>. For n≥125, d(U−L)<L implies (d−1)U<dL≤dC≤dU<(d+1)L, so a gluing must have u+v=d. Only the middle generator can be a convex combination of the other two, and v=d/2−2d/(8n+6) cannot be integral. This proves the cutoff rather than extrapolating. A separate modular-inverse gluing test and an exact Apéry Frobenius/genus calculation both give exactly [2,3,6,7,8,18] over the entire finite interval 2–124.
